source.title: Let's Move!
source.description: Identifica deportes y comprende frases sencillas sobre movimiento y actividad.

grammar.focus: Bloques de presente simple; repaso de can
grammar.explanation: Para hablar de una actividad podemos usar «I + verbo»: «I run». Para expresar capacidad usamos «I can + verbo»: «I can swim». Después de can, el verbo se mantiene en forma básica.
grammar.model: I can swim. I ride a bike.
grammar.practice: Elige el deporte o la acción que corresponde a cada frase.

items.es: Después de can usamos el verbo base swim.
La expresión del currículo es ride a bike.
Basketball es baloncesto.
Con I usamos run, sin -s.

source.readingText: It is Sports Day at school. Ben plays football with his team. Mia plays basketball. Tom likes tennis. After the games, the children run around the field. Mia can swim, and Ben can ride a bike. Everyone moves, plays and has fun.

readingQuestions.question: What day is it at school?
What do the children do on Sports Day?

source.listeningScript: Coach: Welcome to Let's Move! What sport do you like, Ella? Ella: I like tennis. Coach: Can you swim? Ella: Yes, I can. Coach: Can you ride a bike? Ella: Yes, I can. Coach: Great! Ben likes football and basketball. Now let's run to the field and play!

listeningQuestions.question: Which activity does the coach suggest at the end?

grammar.explanation: Usamos «Start» para indicar que una actividad empieza y «Stop» para indicar que debe parar. Como en otras instrucciones, el verbo va al principio y usamos su forma básica.
grammar.model: Start the game. Stop the ball.
grammar.practice: Escucha o lee la regla y elige la instrucción correcta para el juego.

items.prompt: The game is ready. Choose the instruction.
items.es: Start significa empezar.

items.prompt: The ball is moving. Choose the instruction to stop it.
items.es: Stop significa parar.
Team significa equipo.

items.prompt: Which object do you hit in tennis?
items.es: En tenis golpeamos una pelota con la raqueta.

source.readingText: It is Sports Day. Team Blue has a ball and a racket. Team Red has another ball. The teacher says, “Start the game!” The children play and try to win. The ball goes near the goal. The teacher says, “Stop!” The teams listen and wait for the next game.

readingQuestions.question: What does the teacher say first?
What do the children try to do?
What does the teacher say after the ball moves near the goal?
What do the teams do after the instruction?

source.listeningScript: Presenter: Welcome to Sports Day Radio. The teams are ready. Team Green has a ball. Team Yellow has a racket. The teacher says, “Start!” The game begins. The children run to the goal. Then the teacher says, “Stop!” The teams stop and listen. Who will win? Listen and find out!

listeningQuestions.question: What programme are we listening to?
What does the teacher say first?
What does the teacher say next?
What do the teams do after they stop?
Does the presenter tell us who wins?
What is the radio programme about?

grammar.focus: It is a…; nombres de medios de transporte
grammar.explanation: Para identificar un medio de transporte, usamos «It is a…» y el nombre: «It is a bus». La palabra del transporte va después de a.
grammar.model: It is a bus. It is a train.
grammar.practice: Lee cada frase y elige el medio de transporte correcto.

items.es: El modelo es It is + a + transporte.
Car empieza con sonido consonántico; usamos a.
Plane significa avión.

items.prompt: Choose the correct sentence about a taxi.
items.es: Usamos It is a + nombre singular.

source.readingText: It is Transport Town. Mia sees a bus near the school. A car is next to the shop. A train goes past the station. Her brother rides a bike in the park. They see a boat on the river and a plane in the sky. At the end, Mum takes a taxi home.

readingQuestions.question: Where does Mia see a bus?
What is next to the shop?
Which transport moves on the river?

source.listeningScript: Interviewer: Welcome to Transport Town. What can you see, Alex? Alex: I can see a bus and a car. Interviewer: Can you see a train? Alex: Yes, it is near the station. Interviewer: What is in the river? Alex: A boat. Interviewer: And in the sky? Alex: A plane. Interviewer: How do you go home? Alex: I go by taxi.

listeningQuestions.question: Which two vehicles does Alex see first?
Which transport is near a station?

grammar.explanation: «Stop» significa parar y «Go» significa avanzar o ir. Son instrucciones cortas y el verbo aparece al principio. Para esta misión, recuerda: Stop at red. Wait with an adult. Go at green when it is safe.
grammar.model: Stop at red. Go at green.
grammar.practice: Observa el color del semáforo y elige la instrucción adecuada. Sigue siempre las indicaciones de un adulto.

items.prompt: The traffic light is red. What must you do?
items.es: Red significa parar. Espera con un adulto.

items.prompt: The traffic light is green and it is safe. Choose the instruction.
items.es: Go significa avanzar cuando sea seguro y con un adulto.
El modelo del currículo es Stop at red.
Traffic light significa semáforo.

source.readingText: Mia walks with her dad on the street. They come to a traffic light. The light is red. Dad says, “Stop.” They wait together. The light turns green. Dad looks both ways and says, “Now we can go. Stay with me.” Mia holds Dad's hand and they cross safely.

readingQuestions.question: What colour is the light first?
What does Dad say at red?
What do they do while they wait?
What colour does the light turn?
What does Dad do before they go?

source.listeningScript: Ben is with his mum near a road. They stop at the traffic light. The light is red. Mum says, “Stop and wait.” Ben waits next to Mum. The light turns green. Mum looks both ways. She says, “Now we can go. Hold my hand.” Ben and Mum cross the street safely.

listeningQuestions.question: What colour is the light first?
What does Mum tell Ben to do?
What colour does the light turn?
What does Mum do before crossing?
What does Mum ask Ben to hold?
How do they cross the street?

grammar.explanation: Usamos «There is…» para decir que hay un lugar o una cosa. Después ponemos «a» y un nombre singular: «There is a park». En esta misión describimos una ciudad con una frase cada vez.
grammar.model: There is a school. There is a park.
grammar.practice: Observa el plano de la ciudad y elige la frase que corresponde a cada lugar.

items.prompt: Choose the correct sentence about one school.
items.es: Para un lugar singular usamos There is a…
Library es singular; usamos is.
El modelo completo es There is a park.

items.prompt: What does “There is a station” mean?
items.es: There is introduce la existencia de un lugar.

source.readingText: Hello! This is Green Town. There is a school next to the park. There is a library near the station. The supermarket is on Main Street. A small shop is beside the hospital. Children play in the park after school. Green Town is a busy place, and the people like their town.

readingQuestions.question: What is next to the park?
When do children play in the park?
Which place is near the station?
Is Green Town busy or quiet?
Which place sells food and things for the home?
What do the people think about their town?

source.listeningScript: Guide: Welcome to Green Town. Look at the map. There is a school near the park. Visitor: Is there a library? Guide: Yes. There is a library next to the station. Visitor: And the supermarket? Guide: It is on Main Street. There is a hospital beside the shop. Visitor: Thank you. Guide: You're welcome. Enjoy the town!

listeningQuestions.question: What does the visitor say at the end?

grammar.explanation: En una tienda podemos preguntar «How much?» para saber el precio. La palabra «buy» significa comprar. En esta misión usamos «How much?» como pregunta fija y respondemos con una cantidad o un precio muy sencillo.
grammar.practice: Completa un intercambio breve entre el cliente y la persona de la tienda.

items.prompt: Choose the question about the price.
items.es: How much? se usa para preguntar cuánto cuesta.

items.prompt: Complete: I want to ___ a bag.
items.es: Buy es el verbo comprar.
Coin significa moneda.
Podemos pedir el producto y añadir please.

source.readingText: Nina goes to a little shop with Dad. She wants to buy a blue bag. Nina asks, “How much?” The shop worker says, “Two coins.” Dad gives the money. Nina puts the bag in her hand and says, “Thank you.” They leave the shop together.

readingQuestions.question: What does Nina want to buy?
What does Nina do with the bag?
options: She puts it in the river

source.listeningScript: Presenter: Welcome to At the Shops. Listen to this short conversation. Customer: Hello. I want to buy a bag. Worker: What colour? Customer: Blue, please. Worker: Here you are. Customer: How much? Worker: Three coins. Customer: Here is the money. Thank you. Presenter: The customer buys a blue bag for three coins.

listeningQuestions.question: What programme are we listening to?
What does the customer want to buy?
What colour does the customer choose?
What question does the customer ask about the price?
How many coins does the bag cost?
What does the customer give the worker?
What does the customer say at the end?
Who tells us the final price?

source.title: My Home – Where Things Are
source.description: Describe habitaciones y dónde están los objetos con there is, there are y preposiciones.

grammar.explanation: «There is» significa «hay» cuando hablamos de una cosa; «There are» se usa con varias cosas. Para decir dónde está un objeto, añadimos una preposición: «in» (dentro), «on» (sobre), «under» (debajo) o «next to» (al lado).
grammar.model: There is a bed. The book is on the table.
grammar.practice: Elige is o are y después señala la posición correcta del objeto.
grammar.order: The book is on the table.
final: The book is on the table.
The book are on the table.
The book is the table on.

items.es: Bed es una cosa; usamos There is.
Two chairs está en plural; usamos There are.

items.prompt: The book is ___ the table. It touches the top.
items.es: On significa encima de o sobre.

items.prompt: The shoes are ___ the bed. They are below it.
items.es: Under significa debajo de.

source.readingText: Welcome to my home. There is a sofa in the living room. There are two chairs next to the sofa. A book is on the table. There is a lamp next to the sofa. In the bedroom, there is a bed. A blue bag is under the bed. My home is small but nice.

readingQuestions.question: How many chairs are next to the sofa?
What is next to the sofa?
Is the home big or small?
Which sentence uses a plural form?
What does the speaker think about the home?

source.listeningScript: Interviewer: Tell us about your home, Ella. Ella: There is a sofa in the living room. Interviewer: Are there chairs? Ella: Yes, there are two chairs next to the sofa. Interviewer: Where is your book? Ella: It is on the table. Interviewer: And your bag? Ella: It is under my bed. Interviewer: Thank you, Ella.

listeningQuestions.question: Who is talking about the home?
What is in the living room?
Which phrase says there are two chairs?

grammar.focus: Imperativos y verbos de naturaleza en presente simple
grammar.explanation: Usamos el imperativo para dar una instrucción: «Water the flower». Para contar algo que ocurre en la naturaleza, usamos una frase sencilla: «Seeds grow». En esta misión practicamos acciones cortas del jardín.

items.es: El imperativo usa el verbo base water.

source.readingText: On Sunday, Ava works in the garden with Grandpa. There is a big tree and green grass. Ava puts a seed in the soil. Grandpa says, “Water the seed.” A flower grows next to the tree. Ava sees a green leaf and smiles. The garden is full of life.

readingQuestions.question: When does Ava work in the garden?
What is in the garden?
readingQuestions.answer: A big tree and green grass
options: A big tree and green grass

readingQuestions.question: What does Ava put in the soil?
What does Grandpa tell Ava to do?
What grows next to the tree?
What does Ava see on the plant?
How does Ava feel at the end?

source.listeningScript: This is a garden story. Ben finds a seed near a flower. He puts the seed in the soil. His mum says, “Water the seed, please.” Ben gives it water. The sun is warm. After some days, the seed begins to grow. A little leaf appears. Ben is happy. He likes the garden.

listeningQuestions.question: Where does Ben put the seed?
Who tells Ben to water the seed?
What does Ben give the seed?

grammar.focus: There is… e imperativos en una escena
grammar.explanation: «There is…» nos ayuda a decir qué hay en la playa: «There is a shell». Para dar instrucciones usamos un verbo al principio: «Find a shell». Así podemos describir la escena y pedir a alguien que busque un objeto.
grammar.model: There is sand. Find a shell.
grammar.practice: Elige la frase que describe la playa y sigue la instrucción para encontrar un objeto.

items.es: Shell es singular; usamos There is a.
El imperativo usa el verbo base find.
Sand se trata como un nombre no contable en esta frase: There is sand.
Spade significa pala.

source.readingText: It is a sunny day at the beach. Leo has a yellow bucket and a small spade. There is sand near the sea. Leo finds a shell and puts it in the bucket. Mum puts a towel on the sand. The sun is hot, so Leo sits beside Mum and looks at the sea.

readingQuestions.question: What does Leo have with the bucket?
Where does Leo put the shell?
Where does Mum put the towel?
Why does Leo sit beside Mum?

source.listeningScript: Mum: We are at the beach, Ella. Ella: I can see the sea! Mum: Here is your bucket and spade. Ella: Thank you. Mum: Find a shell in the sand. Ella: Look! There is a shell. Mum: Put it in your bucket. Ella: OK. Mum: Now sit on the towel and enjoy the sun.

listeningQuestions.question: Who is at the beach with Ella?
What does Mum ask Ella to find?

grammar.explanation: Preguntamos «What’s the weather like?» para saber qué tiempo hace. Respondemos con «It’s…» y una palabra del tiempo: «It’s sunny», «It’s rainy» o «It’s cold». Podemos escoger una prenda que nos ayude con ese tiempo.
grammar.model: What’s the weather like? It’s rainy.
grammar.practice: Responde a la pregunta del tiempo y elige una prenda apropiada.

items.prompt: Choose the question about the weather.
items.es: Esta es la pregunta modelo del tiempo.
La respuesta usa It is o It’s.

items.prompt: It is rainy. Which item can help keep you dry?
items.es: Un abrigo ayuda cuando llueve o hace frío.

items.prompt: Choose the correct answer: What's the weather like? (cold)
items.es: Respondemos con It's + adjetivo.

source.readingText: Today is rainy and cold in London. Sam looks out of the window. He puts on his coat and boots. His sister has a warm hat. On Sunday, the weather is sunny. Sam wears a hat but not his coat. He asks, “What’s the weather like?” Mum says, “It’s sunny today!”

readingQuestions.question: What is the weather like today?
What does Sam look out of?
What does Sam wear on Sunday?
What is the weather on Sunday?

source.listeningScript: Presenter: Good morning. Here is today's weather report. In the morning, it is rainy and cold. Wear your coat and boots. At lunchtime, the rain stops. In the afternoon, it is sunny. You can wear a hat. Tomorrow is cold again. Thank you for listening to the weather report.

listeningQuestions.question: What is the weather in the morning?
What should people wear in the morning?
What is the weather in the afternoon?
What can people wear in the afternoon?
